newsitem.title: UK: Japanese stocks little changed in quiet London.
newsitem.headline: Japanese stocks little changed in quiet London.

text.p: Japanese stocks were little changed in thin featureless trading in London on Wednesday, with buying interest at a minimum after recent market declines, dealers said.

The Nikkei 50 index of leading stocks trading here was up 0.6 points or 0.04 percent at 1,584.39. In Tokyo the Nikkei 225 in Tokyo closed 156.72 points or 0.8 percent lower at 19,697.17. -- continuing a retreat from its year's high of 20,910.79 set on June 26.
Dealers said stocks could stage a limited rebound in Tokyo on Thursday but there was no reason to think the recent downtrend would bottom out in the short term.

One dealer at a Japanese brokerage in London said recent profit-taking in blue chips, linked with worries about Japanese corporate bankruptcies and a recent rebound in the yen, was likely to deter foreign buyers for the time being.
"There might be a bit of a squeeze back in the market on Thursday," the dealer said, "but there is no reason to steam in agressively."
Toyota fell to 3,227.5 yen from a close of 3,240.0 yen in Tokyo while Sumitomo Bank was quoted up at 1,742.5 compared with a Tokyo close of 1,740.0 yen.
